name: Ventilator-Induced Diaphragmatic Dysfunction

prevalence.estimate: unknown, occurs in up to 50% of mechanically ventilated patients

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No standardized formal criteria; diagnosis based on clinical and diagnostic findings

criteria.description: History of prolonged mechanical ventilation (>48 hours)
Objective evidence of diaphragmatic weakness or reduced contractility on ultrasonography or phrenic nerve stimulation
Exclusion of other neuromuscular disorders causing diaphragm dysfunction
Decreased tidal volume or respiratory muscle strength during spontaneous breathing trials

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of prolonged mechanical ventilation plus objective evidence of diaphragmatic weakness and exclusion of other neuromuscular causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires integration of clinical, imaging, and electrophysiological data.

searchTerms: defect or malformation of diaphragm muscle

pathognomonic.symptomName: Ventilator dependence with inability to wean

searchTerms: EMG showing nerve or muscle problems
reduced breathing in with maximal effort

occasional.symptomName: Respiratory insufficiency due to muscle weakness
searchTerms: respiratory insufficiency due to muscle weakness
difficulty breathing caused by muscle weakness

laboratory: Arterial blood gases showing hypoxemia and/or hypercapnia
Elevated inflammatory markers secondary to critical illness
imaging: Ultrasound evidence of reduced diaphragmatic thickness and contractility
Chest X-ray may show elevated hemidiaphragm
genetic: No known genetic mutations directly associated
other: Phrenic nerve stimulation tests showing reduced diaphragmatic response

distinguishingFeatures: History of nerve injury or surgery
Absent or reduced phrenic nerve conduction
Fluctuating muscle weakness including ocular muscles

redFlags: Failure to wean from mechanical ventilation after prolonged support
Rapid progression of respiratory muscle weakness
Development of respiratory failure requiring tracheostomy
references: Jaber S, Petrof BJ, Jung B, et al. Rapidly progressive diaphragmatic weakness and injury during mechanical ventilation in humans. Am J Respir Crit Care Med. 2011;183(3):364-371.
Levine S, Nguyen T, Taylor N, et al. Rapid disuse atrophy of diaphragm fibers in mechanically ventilated humans. N Engl J Med. 2008;358(13):1327-1335.
Goligher EC, Dres M, Fan E, et al. Mechanical ventilation-induced diaphragm atrophy strongly impacts clinical outcomes. Am J Respir Crit Care Med. 2018;197(2):204-213.
